newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRIDAY'S FRENCH FIRST DIVISION MATCHES. [CORRECTED 13:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRIDAY'S FRENCH FIRST DIVISION MATCHES. [CORRECTED 13:20 GMT]

text.p: Matches in the French first division on Friday (league positions in brackets, all 1800 GMT kickoff):
Bastia (4) v Lens (11)

New stand opens at Bastia's Furiani ground where 17 people were killed when a temporary stand collapsed during a cup game in 1992 opens (corrects from "killed in a riot..."). Capacity boosted to 10,500. Lens, deprived through injury of winger Tony Vairelles but with defender Frederic Dehu back from suspension, seek second successive win.
Rennes (10) v Paris St Germain (1)

France goalkeeper Bernard Lama and defender Bruno N'Gotty return after injury to bolster leaders' rearguard after lean spell with defeat in UEFA Cup and draw at home to Auxerre. They face striker Stephane Guivarc'h, on loan to Rennes from Auxerre and surprise top scorer in the division.
Nice (19) v Cannes (14)

Riviera derby in which Nice, who have conceded average of two goals per match, need desperately to reverse alarming slump that has seen them plunge to one from bottom. Italian Roberto Onorati still doubtful with thigh injury.
Auxerre (3) v Lyon (9)

Champions could be without captain Sabri Lamouchi (ankle strain) and defender Alain Goma (thigh). But winger Bernard Diomede, bane of Grasshopper Zurich defence last week, returns after missing weekend trip to Paris.
Lille (5) v Monaco (2)

In-form Monaco, who scored four goals in each of their last European and domestic games, visit surprise side Lille, fifth and unbeaten at home, in match of day. Yugoslav Miladin Becanovic and Djezon Boutoille return after suspension to boost Lille attack.
Metz (6) v Le Havre (15)

Metz, who visit Sporting Lisbon with 2-0 first leg lead in their UEFA Cup tie next week, play without suspended Cameroon defender Rigobert Song. Northern port side welcome back former France under-21 midfielder Nicolas Huysman from injury.
Marseille (12) v Nantes (16)

Former European champions look to redeem themselves with Velodrome crowd after shock 1-0 defeat by lowly Caen in last home game. Nantes, back in form with more goals scored than any other team in division, are unbeaten in six matches.
Strasbourg (7) v Nancy (20)
Strasbourg look to bounce back after 3-0 defeat at Caen last weekend ended four-match winning run. Northern Ireland forward Phil Gray is doubtful for Nancy after injury in 0-0 draw with Marseille.
Caen (18) v Guingamp (13)

Caen, who have strung together first two wins of season, face Guingamp side who bagged UEFA Cup place in first season in top flight but struggling to halt slump in second. Guingamp have captain Lionel Rouxel suspended but France defender Vincent Candela and Liberia striker Christopher Wreh back after suspension.
Playing Thursday night: Bordeaux (8) v Montpellier (17)
